newsitem.title: UK: LME responds to SIB review, sets out timetable.
newsitem.headline: LME responds to SIB review, sets out timetable.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) delivered its resonse on Thursday to the recent Securities and Investments Board (SIB) review of the market and set out how it will implement SIB's proposals.

"The LME has passed to the SIB a detailed implementation programme addressing each of the recommendations made by the SIB and indicating how the LME plans to go about implementation," the LME said in a release.
"LME's Board of Directors has very carefully considered the recommendations put forward by the SIB and is intent on implementing those...on a timely basis," it added.

The LME will consult further with members, market-users, and others over coming weeks. The timeframe for implementation depends on the issue being addressed, and dates vary between January 1997, through 1997 to the year-end, it said.
The Exchange has also established an Implementation Task Force comprising a number of Board members and chaired by LME Chairman Raj Bagri or Chief Executive David King.

Two further sub-committees have been set up as well - a regulatory issues sub-committee and a warehousing issues sub-committee, chaired respectively by Kit Farrow and Philip Crowson, two invited Board members.
In its release the LME said that there were two key factors arising from the SIB report.
There was a clear endorsement from LME users that they like the way the Exchange works and have no aspiration to seek fundamental change.
Also, there was a clear endorsement from SIB that it has identified no clear risk arising from the way the LME operates.
The SIB, Britain's top regulator was asked by the LME to carry out a wide-ranging review of the market after the Sumitomo Corp scandal shocked world markets in June 1996.
In mid-June, Sumitomo fired its head copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he had admitted running up losses of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trading.
